cards.back: 10M documents from 3 sources, 50k employees, about 100 questions/s at peak. First token under 2 s, full answer under 8 s.
Mostly a fixed workflow. The model makes exactly one decision: whether to rewrite the query and search once more when nothing relevant was found.
A document ID, not a chunk. A webhook is only a hint; the worker always fetches the latest version and compares versions, so duplicates and reordering are harmless.
Write the new version's chunks first (IDs like doc_id#version#n), then delete every older-version chunk for that doc_id. An ACL change only rewrites metadata.
10M documents at about 50 docs/s per connector is 200,000 s, about 2.3 days. It runs in a separate lane that shares the quota but reserves headroom for live updates.
About 50M chunks at 768 float32 dimensions, about 3 KB each, is roughly 150 GB of vectors, so a sharded, managed index.
Never mix two models in one index. Build a second index, backfill, eval both, swap blue-green and keep the old one for rollback.
Auth ~50 ms, rewrite ~300 ms, hybrid retrieval ~150 ms to a top 50, rerank ~200 ms to the best 8, permission recheck ~20 ms, then about 1 s to first token.
Embeddings blur exact tokens like ticket IDs and error codes; BM25 catches them. Merge both with reciprocal rank fusion.
Apply the permission filter inside the vector and keyword queries, not after, or the model answers from the few weak chunks left. Recheck before the prompt and fail closed.
60% resolved, 80% thumbs-up, 95% grounded, 85% recall@10, p95 8 s, under $0.02 per question, zero permission leaks.

quiz.q: Users with narrow access get thin, vague answers, while admins get good ones. Retrieval takes the top 20 and then removes chunks the user cannot see. What do you change?
choices: Apply the permission filter inside the vector and keyword queries
Give the model the ACLs to decide
quiz.why: Filtering after retrieval leaves the model a few weak chunks; filtering inside the search ranks only permitted chunks.

quiz.q: Latency to first token doubled after a reranker change. Which step do you check first in the trace?
choices: The rerank span: how many candidates it scores and its time against the ~200 ms budget
quiz.why: One trace per request with a span per step shows which stage blew its share of the budget.

quiz.q: A search for 'HR-4512' returns unrelated policy pages. What is missing?
quiz.why: Embeddings blur exact identifiers; hybrid search catches them on keywords.

quiz.q: A webhook was missed and an edited page stays stale for hours. What catches it?
choices: The hourly reconciliation crawl over each source's change feed
quiz.why: Webhooks give speed; the crawl gives correctness.

quiz.q: During the backfill, a slow worker writes v3 of a doc after a live edit already wrote v4. What happens?
choices: The v3 write is rejected because writes only go through when the version is newer
v3 overwrites v4 until the next crawl
Both versions are kept and the reranker picks one
quiz.why: Version-checked writes reject late, older writes.

quiz.q: Someone reports a wrong expense limit. The trace shows the right document was retrieved and cited. Where is the problem?
choices: Prompt or model: it misused a correct source
quiz.why: If retrieval found the right document, the failure is in how the model used it.

quiz.q: The team wants to swap to a new embedding model. What is the safe path?
choices: Re-embed in place, document by document
Mix old and new vectors and let the reranker sort it out
Change the model and run evals next week
Build a second index, backfill it, eval both, then swap blue-green and keep the old one
quiz.why: Never mix vectors from two models in one index.
